reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 is about magnetocaloric materials and is irrelevant. E2 shows nano-twinning enhances toughness in a medium-entropy alloy but does not link this to short-range ordering or heat treatment. E3 discusses stacking fault energy and twinning but does not connect them to controlled heat treatment or ordering. The core mechanistic chain from heat treatment to ordering to SFE variation to toughness is unsupported.
premises: Controlled heat treatment can induce a moderate degree of short-range atomic ordering in HEAs.
Short-range ordering creates local variations in stacking fault energy.
Local stacking fault energy variations promote nano-twinning and enhanced dislocation mobility.
Nano-twinning and enhanced dislocation mobility improve toughness.
Excessive heat treatment leads to brittle intergranular precipitates or over-homogenization, reducing toughness.
